purpose: Compare the live materialized second literal of the real Prim-68 reproducer immediately before vm_codebuf takeover and immediately after the owner reload.

literal_1.semantic_requirement: The little-endian word is a SYMI whose live target name is %is.

derivation: expected must be a SYMI whose live target name is %is

checkpoints.meaning: Prim 68 has been selected; vm_codebuf has not yet been invalidated or overwritten by the overlay-call context.
The full owner header reload returned successfully; literal-table pointer setup and literal consumption have not begun.

hardware_procedure: Build one SHA-bound nonpromotable diagnostic identity from Link 74 with both patches and with all affected carrier, record, payload and product identities rebound; do not relink.
Boot to the REPL and run the real %is Prim-68 reproducer.
At PC $1e8f capture the code header, LIT(1), owner cells and c2_runtime three times; derive the independent expected word from the live C2D entry and resolution planes.
Restore bytes a9 33 80 at $1e8f in live memory and resume without rebooting, retaining the same live session entry.
At PC $543b capture the same cells three times. No resume is required.
Discard the diagnostic identity after adjudication; it is never promotable.

decision.transport_or_materialization_fault: Either materialized LIT(1) sample differs from the independently derived live C2D expected word. Initial mismatch indicts initial materialization/read; initial match plus reload mismatch indicts post-service owner reload or its physical transport.
decision.transport_correct_consumption_fault: The live C2D expected word, initial LIT(1), and reloaded LIT(1) are byteidentical, and the word is the SYMI named %is. Physical materialization, ownership and reload are then excluded; the remaining fault is literal selection or dir_find consumption after reload.

claim_limit: This document prequalifies one exact target-only discriminator. It records no hardware result, changes no product byte, creates no product link and makes no promotion claim.
